source_text: So, one applied idea where the small-causal diagram idea could be *practical*.  I know we are still trying to check whether it even works at all.  But suppose we want a "policy for selecting the next M-E-T-A- task to work on" ... that's what codex-10 is currently writing.  We could validate *that* with our Fong-inspired approach rather than waiting for the WM itself to produce a cascade.

reply_text:
㊥ (checking codex-10's META policy) This works, and it has already found a gap. I read codex-10's draft, `futon3/library/meta/meta-outer-policy-cascade.edn`, which is still uncommitted. I wrote its four patterns as small causal models and joined them. They join cleanly, and the model answers "what gets selected?" for three states of the machine:
- **Healthy:** ordinary M/E/T work is selected.
- **Injured, with a repair algorithm on file:** the self-heal (A) arm is selected.
- **Injured, with no matching repair algorithm:** neither arm admits anything, so nothing is selected.

That third case is an abstention, which you ruled out on 2026-09-29. The draft's guards don't cover it, and the WM didn't have to run for us to find it.

㊢ (how) The models follow the draft's own `:arms` guards:
- `observe-the-meta-field` produces the field census and the injury observation;
- `fill-meta-policy-slots` produces the ordinary arm (field non-empty and no injury);
- `injury-routes-to-self-heal` produces the self-heal arm (injury and a matching repair algorithm);
- `minimise-g-over-filled-meta-policies` selects if either arm has candidates.

The join's only external inputs are the META field, the injury state and whether a matching repair algorithm exists. The declared precedence matches the data dependencies, so there's no "support is not precedence" conflict here. The script is in `/tmp/meta_outer_glue.clj`. I haven't committed it, because codex-10 is still editing those files.

🈖 (why this is practical) The method checks a policy's structure before it is ever run:
- Do the guards cover every state?
- Does an injury really exclude M/E/T work?
- Does each output depend only on what it should?

The third case shows the value: injured, with nothing on file to repair it. The fix is codex-10's to choose. One option is a third arm whose A item is "write or find the missing repair algorithm". Another is to let ordinary work through with the injury recorded. The draft's `:rearm-slot` on the self-heal arm is the WR-26 card on these turns put into practice: when ordinary work is switched off, the condition for switching it back on is written at the switch.

㊟ (limits) This checks only the structure of the selection, true or false. It doesn't check G: whether the predicted outcomes and preferences rank the filled policies sensibly is a separate question. The draft is still changing, so its next version may already close the gap.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I send codex-10 the missing-arm finding, with the three cases, as a bell into its current work?

previous_reply_acts.text:
(what changed) Commit `6d579cfe`:
- **`agreement_record.clj`** reads the 🈸 paragraphs out of a reply and builds an offer from them. Each paragraph becomes one numbered option, with the paragraph text as its label. The offer is dated at the reply and keyed to it, so it is minted only once.
- **The agreement route** falls back to that offer only when it would otherwise refuse with `no-visible-offer`. It checks that the reply is this seat's own assistant turn in the same session. It still requires the agent's offer grant, so the route can't make offers for an agent that couldn't make them itself.
- **The mission** M-aif-over-the-operator now notes that the "agents post an offer for each 🈸" item is mostly met from the reading side (commit `e32a2181`).

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what I checked)
- **Tests:** four new tests, covering one ask, several asks, no ask, and that the minted offer passes offer validation. 10 tests, 49 assertions pass, and clj-kondo is clean.
- **Live:** the two namespaces were reloaded from master, and the agents route still answers 200. The replay took 32 s, most of it waiting on futon1b.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(two things to know)
- **Earlier refusals stay on record.** The older refusals are still recorded alongside the new agreement. The earlier `🈸:yes` for the held-out test hasn't been replayed. I can do that if you want the record complete.
- **"Informally: yes please" still won't parse.** By design, only `yes` with an optional number or offer id counts, so that ordinary replies don't trigger agreements. So that turn was handled as conversation, not as an agreement.
